intro: The AI industry is swimming in money and drowning in contradictions. OpenAI just raised $11 billion at a staggering $1.25 trillion valuation — even as midterm voters signaled deep skepticism about AI's unchecked expansion — while a new METR report from inside Anthropic reveals AI development is accelerating twice as fast as last year, with the technology increasingly building itself. Today's digest is a snapshot of an industry sprinting forward on every front: Google pouring $17 billion into data centers, data center developers quietly abandoning their green energy promises, China allegedly planting spies near Nvidia's CEO, and a major blockchain firm exposing FBI credentials to hackers.

stories.title: Chainalysis discloses major breach exposing credentials for all customers including FBI and Microsoft
stories.summary: Blockchain analysis firm Chainalysis disclosed a breach in which hackers stole credentials, password hashes, and live authentication tokens for all customers, including government agencies (FBI, ICE, US Air Force) and companies (Microsoft, Coinbase, Barclays). The company described AI agent-assisted offensive techniques and an on-path attack. Chainalysis took down its login page and is requiring mandatory credential rotation, but key details remain unanswered including the attack source and why disclosure was delayed two days.
stories.opinion: The involvement of AI-assisted offensive techniques marks an escalation in real-world cyberattacks, and the high-profile customer list—especially law enforcement and intelligence agencies—makes this breach exceptionally consequential for national security.

stories.title: Steve Jones cartoon comments on dangerous technology innovations
stories.summary: The Guardian published a Steve Jones editorial cartoon on November 7, 2026, commenting on dangerous technology innovations including AI. The cartoon itself is only viewable on the Guardian's website.
stories.opinion: An editorial cartoon with no substantive news content beyond cultural commentary on tech anxieties.

stories.title: Crusoe sells troubled Wyoming data center project to Google for $17 billion investment
stories.summary: Denver-based data center developer Crusoe (valued at $30.9 billion) sold its unfinished Wyoming data center project to Google, which plans to invest $17 billion to develop the campus. Crusoe had originally announced the project with Blackstone-backed Tallgrass with plans to scale to 10 gigawatts. Google had reportedly raised concerns about cost and timeline under Crusoe's management. Crusoe continues to work with Google on a separate Texas project and counts Oracle, OpenAI, Microsoft, Meta, and Jane Street among its clients.
stories.opinion: Google swooping in on a troubled project it was already scrutinizing suggests the hyperscalers are gaining even more leverage over independent data center developers—Crusoe's $30.9B valuation may not insulate it from being a build-to-sell operation for bigger players.

stories.title: METR report on Anthropic's AI-accelerated development draws alarm from researchers
stories.summary: METR conducted an 11-week investigation inside Anthropic and found AI development is progressing roughly twice as fast as a year ago, with AI driving most of the acceleration. Anthropic was allowed to redact portions of the report, raising transparency concerns. The findings come as Anthropic prepares to go public while CEO Dario Amodei has called for labs to slow down, highlighting tensions between commercial ambitions and safety rhetoric.
stories.opinion: The Verge's framing emphasizes the tension between Anthropic's safety messaging and its commercial trajectory, and highlights the transparency problem of allowing a subject to redact its own evaluation—a dynamic that undermines the credibility of third-party safety auditing. Where coverage differs: The Rundown AI (yesterday:4) reports specific figures including AI responsible for 80% of acceleration, two unreleased internal models, and a 'Model 4' clearing 50% on all 15 benchmarks; The Verge does not include these specifics but adds context about Amodei calling for labs to slow down and Anthropic's upcoming IPO

stories.title: Lanarkshire AI data centre abandons renewables pledge, will draw entirely from National Grid
stories.summary: DataVita, a data centre company central to the UK's AI strategy, has admitted its massive 1GW AI development near Glasgow will be entirely powered by the National Grid, reversing its original promise to use renewable energy equivalent to the output of a small nuclear reactor or Britain's largest windfarm.
stories.opinion: This reversal exposes a pattern where data centre developers use green energy pledges to win planning approvals, then quietly switch to grid power—undermining both climate commitments and public trust in AI infrastructure projects.

stories.title: OpenAI raises $11 billion at $1.25 trillion valuation as AI funding landscape shifts post-midterms
stories.summary: OpenAI has raised $11 billion in a new funding round valuing the company at $1.25 trillion, making it one of the world's most valuable companies. The round was scaled back from an originally larger target due to declining tech stocks and midterm election results reflecting public opposition to AI and data centers. The round hasn't closed and is expected to total about $20 billion. Meanwhile, Anthropic has filed to go public, and OpenAI has delayed its own IPO plans. The broader AI market faces uncertainty following the Democratic midterm landslide.
stories.opinion: The scaled-back raise signals that even the AI sector's biggest name isn't immune to market headwinds—post-midterm regulatory uncertainty and declining public sentiment toward AI infrastructure are now directly constraining valuations and fundraising ambitions. Where coverage differs: TechCrunch reports the target was $30 billion (per late September reports); The Verge specifies the target was $30 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation TechCrunch reports Anthropic's IPO valuation expectations dropped to ~$1.1 trillion from $2 trillion; The Verge says only that Anthropic filed its S-1 The Verge notes a prior $122 billion raise in March 2026 at $852 billion valuation; TechCrunch does not mention this prior round

stories.title: Southeast Asia's data centre boom hits wall as power and water constraints mount
stories.summary: Southeast Asia's data centre expansion is stalling as power and water constraints create obstacles. Thailand, which had approved $27 billion in data centre projects from TikTok, UAE-based Skyline, and Singapore's Bridge datacentres earlier in 2026, has seen momentum halt. The region is facing practical limits of its energy and water resources.
stories.opinion: This is the supply-side reality check the AI infrastructure buildout was always heading toward—approving billions in projects is easy, but the physics of power generation and water supply don't scale on venture timelines.

stories.title: Meta introduces Spaces for Muse agents, adding project-specific collaboration threads
stories.summary: Meta launched Spaces, a feature for its Muse AI agents that lets users create topic-specific conversation threads for projects like vacation planning or gift tracking. Spaces integrate with third-party apps and auto-update with new information. CEO Zuckerberg demonstrated uses including event tracking and home control. This follows Muse Voice for verbal commands. Meta reported 10 million Muse users in the US and Canada less than two months after launch.
stories.opinion: The 10 million user figure in under two months is notable, and Spaces' third-party app integration positions Muse as a platform play rather than just a chatbot—though the actual utility of persistent AI project threads remains unproven at scale.

stories.title: China reportedly recruited AI executive to spy on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
stories.summary: China's Ministry of State Security reportedly recruited Alice Huang, an executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed, to spy on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and gather intelligence about American AI chips, potentially to influence Nvidia to make advanced chips available to China. Alice Huang has close relationships with top AI chip industry executives. President Trump was briefed last year but took no action. Three House committees have asked Jensen Huang to appear for a closed-door briefing. The two Huangs are not related but are described as having a 'close' relationship.
stories.opinion: This story sits at the intersection of AI chip export controls, espionage, and Congressional oversight—the fact that Trump was briefed and took no action will likely become the political flashpoint, especially given ongoing debates about China AI chip restrictions.

tweet_headlines.author: DD_Nanall
tweet_headlines.headline: KeyDeck's new MCP integration __shows AI your project's key names but never the keys themselves__, requiring Touch ID approval before writing any .env.
tweet_headlines.source_text:
I wasn't going to add MCP to KeyDeck.

Someone asked for it on my last post, and my first thought was: what's the downside? Letting an AI near your API keys felt wrong. Anything you paste into an AI chat goes to the AI company. That's exactly what KeyDeck exists to stop.

Then I found a way to do it without that risk.

How it works:

• KeyDeck runs a small connection on your Mac, only while it's open. Nothing on the internet can reach it.
• You connect Claude Code, Cursor or VS Code in one click (or one line for Claude Code).
• Your AI can see your project names and which keys exist, like "Stripe, Supabase, Claude". Never the keys themselves.
• When it needs your .env, a popup asks you first. You approve with Touch ID, and KeyDeck writes the file into your project.
• The AI only hears "done, 5 keys written."
• It can't add, change or delete anything in KeyDeck.
• Each AI tool gets its own connection key, so you can cut one off without touching the others.

So it's in.

KeyDeck: every API key in one locked place, now with an AI that can set up your project without ever seeing your keys.

tweet_headlines.author: PawelHuryn
tweet_headlines.headline: Pawel Huryn argues __every AI knowledge system degrades without regular pruning__ and proposes a /dream command to merge duplicates and delete stale notes.
tweet_headlines.source_text:
Learn from this. Just don't hand your agent's memory to a lab.

I've been doing a lot of this with plain .md files for months. One small index the agent always loads. Domain files it opens only when a task needs them. It's in my repo, so I can read it, diff it, fix it, and the same files work in Codex.

Even Claude Code's own memory loads just the first 200 lines, as an index.

Their tests back the rest:

- Better models keep less.
- Telling the model how to write memory hurt. Say what memory is for, then let it judge.
- Check notes regularly. They call it dreaming.

I added a /dream to Mini Harness this week: merge duplicates, delete what the code contradicts, keep the index accurate. Without it, every knowledge system degrades over time.

tweet_headlines.author: ShaneHummus
tweet_headlines.headline: Shane Hummus says he automates __90% of his content with Claude__ — from VidIQ idea research to thumbnail mockups, 10 titles, and full scripts in one session.
tweet_headlines.source_text:
How I automate 90% of my content with Claude:

1. Niche: You tell Claude your field, what you know, and what people ask you about. It asks you questions, then hands back a few options in one sentence (e.g., I help X do Y).

2. Video idea: Claude searches VidIQ and TubeLab for videos with 100,000 views or more from channels with 100,000 subscribers or less, at 5 views per subscriber or better. The video itself should be mediocre or preferably bad, because a weak video that still wins proves the idea carried it.

3. Title, thumbnail, and intro: Claude gives you a thumbnail mockup, 10 titles, 5 thumbnail text options, and 5 intros for that idea. Pick one title, one thumbnail, and one intro that tell the same story, because congruence beats quality every single time.

4. Script: Start with a yap session, where you talk to Claude for 5 to 10 minutes about your stories, your numbers, and your mistakes. Claude writes the outline and the word-for-word script from that, and your voice is what keeps it from sounding like AI slop.

5. Recording: If you have a personal brand channel, you're going to be recording yourself. Your phone or your laptop webcam is more than enough to get started.

6. Editing: Claude can edit through the Descript connector, but on a 5-minute video it took 28 minutes and still lost to a 3-minute edit by hand. Edit the transcript yourself in Descript, deleting what you don't want like you are editing a Google Doc.

7. Analytics: Download your YouTube analytics, drop them into Claude, and have it find what went right instead of what went wrong. Your winners are stronger proof than anybody else's video ever will be.

8. Syndication: Cut one long video into shorts and written posts for LinkedIn, Instagram, and Facebook. It only works in that direction, because a LinkedIn post has nothing in it to cut into a video.

tweet_headlines.author: Zephyr_hg
tweet_headlines.headline: Nine Claude prompt skills worth bookmarking: /anti-ai __strips em-dashes and AI giveaway words__, /grill-me tightens vagueness, /write-a-skill packages prompts you reuse.
tweet_headlines.source_text:
My 9 (most-used) Claude Skills to write prompts.

The full list is in the card →

Everything below is what you'll get:

1. /brief - turns a brain-dump into a clean task spec before Claude runs anything.

2. /grill-me - keeps asking until nothing is vague. The prompt fixes itself in the answers.

3. /how-to - for when I don't even know what to ask. Maps the steps first, then we prompt.

4. /sonnet-tune - rewrites the optimised prompt for Sonnet. Models read differently.

5. /opus-tune - same job, tuned for Opus. Two models, two ways of prompting.

6. /personal-voice - bakes my STYLE.md into the prompt. Outputs sound like me on the first try.

7. /anti-ai - strips the em-dashes and the dead giveaway AI words before they ever appear.

8. /write-a-skill - turns any prompt I reuse into a new Skill. The library builds itself.

9. /handoff - compresses the whole chat into the opening prompt of the next one. Nothing gets lost.

Stop rewriting the same prompt from scratch. Turn the ones that work into Skills once, then stack them.

Add each one in Claude → Settings → Skills.
